title: Peanut Chutney Roti Roll
subtitle: Whole wheat roti rolled around a coarse, spiced peanut chutney.
protein: ~18–22g protein per adult (2 rolls) — peanuts + wheat

nightPrep.label: Night Before
items: Make the dry peanut chutney (step 1) — it keeps for weeks, so one batch covers many mornings
Optionally make the dough for the rotis — keeps overnight in the fridge

method.title: Make dry chutney (~10 min)
items: Pulse {@peanuts} in a dry blender — 5–6 short pulses until coarse crumble; do not over-blend into paste
Add {@cumin}, {@hing}, {@salt} and {@aamchur}; pulse 2–3 times — keep it coarse and sandy, not smooth
Set aside {=¼ cup} in a small jar for the toddler now, before the chili goes in
Add {@red-chili} to the rest; pulse 2–3 more times to combine
Store both in airtight jars — 2–3 weeks at room temperature

method.title: Morning assembly
items: Heat {@roti:adult|rotis} on tawa — 30 sec per side; smear {@ghee} on each while warm
Spread {@chutney:roll} over each roti — if too dry, mix in {@yogurt-spread:roll} first
Roll tightly and serve immediately or wrap in foil

method.label: Toddler version
items: Use her chili-free chutney from the small jar
Mix {@chutney:toddler} with {@yogurt-spread:toddler} to make a mild creamy spread
Spread on {@roti:toddler|soft roti} cut into strips or small pieces — easier for her to manage than a roll
Add {@paneer:toddler|soft paneer pieces} or {@cucumber:toddler|thinly sliced cucumber} inside

method.label: Tip
method.text: The chutney is the protein workhorse here — 2 tbsp of dry peanut chutney has ~7–8g protein. Double-layer it for more flavor and protein.
